# CAD-to-CAD Strengthens Officer Safety in High-Speed Pursuit


October 29, 2026


by Jillian Donley


##


In emergency response, information sharing can be just as critical as manpower.


## A Critical Incident Crosses County Lines


When a dual-county pursuit escalated into an officer-involved shooting in southern Michigan, dispatchers in Lenawee and Jackson counties relied on CAD-to-CAD to share real-time updates and maintain situational awareness throughout the response.


The incident began in Lenawee County, where a family called 911 from a local hospital to report that one brother had shot another brother in the hand. With the suspect's location unknown, dispatchers in Lenawee distributed a be-on-the-lookout (BOL) alert and shared the information with neighboring Jackson County.


## Putting CAD-to-CAD to the Test


For Lenawee County, the incident also served as an early test of the technology's capabilities. The communications center had only recently begun using CAD-to-CAD when the call occurred.


"This was actually kind of our first go-around with the CAD-to-CAD," Lenawee County 911 Director Lt. Chris Hudson said. "We utilized it rather quickly in a major incident call."


The value of intercounty connectivity became evident later that evening when Jackson County deputies located the suspect vehicle.


"We sent out a BOL to Jackson as well," Hudson explained. "And later in the night, Jackson actually came across that vehicle, which led them on a high-speed pursuit."


## Real-Time Visibility During a High-Risk Pursuit


As the pursuit unfolded, the situation escalated rapidly. The suspect threw pipe bombs at and fired on law enforcement in Jackson County, resulting in an officer-involved shooting in which both an officer and the suspect were struck.


Throughout the incident, CAD-to-CAD gave both agencies a shared view of developments as the situation evolved.


"With the CAD-to-CAD, we were able to watch and monitor that pursuit by the notes that were put in the CAD," Hudson said.


"We did not need to call them and bother them in the middle of a high-stress situation. We did not have to listen to their radio as they were entering information into their call. It was automatically being transferred to Lenawee so that we could monitor the situation and know what was exactly going on with our suspect."


## Enhancing Officer Safety With Faster Information Sharing


As the response expanded beyond Lenawee County, the CAD-to-CAD connection helped ensure that personnel involved from the beginning stayed informed as the situation continued to evolve and new details emerged.


"All of our information was being put in that call," Jackson County 911 Deputy Director Mallory Fugate recalled. "The units that were investigating their initial call knew what they were walking into coming into Jackson."


"It is a huge officer safety benefit," Hudson added.


The real-time flow of information also ensured that personnel in Lenawee stayed prepared for the possibility of the suspect reentering their jurisdiction.


"If the suspect had gone, turned out of our city and headed back south, they knew what was coming in their direction," Fugate explained. "Everything was being passed along up to the minute, and they never once called us to bother us. They had units that were monitoring their radio system; they could see what was going on."


## Maintaining Situational Awareness Without Additional Calls


For neighboring counties, maintaining situational awareness during an event of that scale would have previously required a series of phone call updates between communications centers.


"Before, if they got into this pursuit, I as a dispatcher would probably call up to Jackson," Hudson shared. "As they're talking on the radio, repeating the pursuit information, they're also talking to me on the phone."


This time, dispatchers were able to monitor developments in real time without disrupting response coordination with calls back and forth to their neighboring county.


"\[CAD-to-CAD\] alleviates a lot of that stress of trying to keep your neighboring jurisdictions informed," Hudson said.


## Why CAD-to-CAD Matters for Multi-Jurisdictional Response


For Jackson and Lenawee counties, the incident highlighted how real-time information-sharing capabilities through CAD-to-CAD can help neighboring agencies maintain situational awareness and coordinate their response when critical events extend beyond a single jurisdiction.
